Bar length shows the time, to scale. Your card's minimum formula may differ: check the box on your own statement.

slides.title: Read the *warning box*
slides.prompt: Here is the minimum payment box from my card statement, account number blacked out. In plain words: how long will paying only the minimum take, what will it cost in total, and what monthly payment clears it in 3 years?
slides.why: Your statement must show this box. It assumes you add no new purchases.

slides.title: Rehearse the *call*
slides.prompt: Play a card company rep. I am calling to ask for a lower APR. Push back like a real rep would. After the call, tell me what to say better and what I should write down.
slides.why: Practice first. Then ask about a hardship program: some lower the rate or waive fees for a while.

slides.title: Pick your *order*
slides.prompt: Here are my cards with balance, APR and minimum payment. With $[amount] a month in total, compare paying the highest APR first versus the smallest balance first: months to debt free and total interest for each.
slides.why: Highest APR first usually saves the most interest. Smallest balance first gives quicker wins.

slides.title: Test the *transfer*
slides.prompt: Here is a balance transfer offer. Work out the fee, how much I would still owe when the intro rate ends on [date] if I pay $[amount] a month, and what that leftover costs at the regular APR.
slides.why: Fees are usually 3% to 5%. Whatever is left when the promo ends gets the card's regular APR.

slides.title: Answer a *collector*
slides.prompt: A debt collector sent me this letter, my details blacked out. List who they say I owe, how much, and the dispute deadline. Then draft a short letter asking them to verify the debt.
slides.why: You usually have 30 days to dispute in writing. Miss it and you can lose some rights.

bg_facts: Your statement shows what paying only the minimum costs.
Balance transfer fees are usually 3% to 5%.
Highest APR first usually saves the most interest.
You usually have 30 days to dispute a collection in writing.
